content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I discovered that the firmware needed upgrading for the later [article_no] version of the [product_name]. I'm trying to upload from a Mac but received a message saying I need a newer version of [product_name] software. Can anyone assist? I downloaded the upgrade from the official site but received a message in the attached image. Much appreciated. [user_name]
Hi [user_name], do you mean you downloaded it from this site? [product_name] demo software, upgrades/updates, drivers ... - [company_name]
Yes, that's correct, it was from that site.

Hello [user_name], • Download update_v7_1_5.luf • Change the file name to update_v7_1_5.rar and extract it • From the extracted folder, copy the classes.jar file • Locate your installed [product_name] software folder, find the classes.jar file in the lib directory, then replace it with the one you extracted. • You're good to go! Note: It's smart to backup the original file in case something goes wrong. Hope this helps!
Thank you for the guidance, that solution worked right away. Much appreciated. [user_name]
Happy to hear the issue’s resolved.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced compatibility issues between their version of [product_name] software and a newer [product_name] module ([article_no] version), especially when uploading from a Mac. The software requested an update, and even after downloading it from the official site, users struggled to apply it. A workaround provided by another user resolved the issue, highlighting that the upgrade process is not always straightforward and support for Mac users could be improved.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expected updates for [product_name] software to be simple and immediately compatible with the required module version when obtained from the official [company_name] site, particularly on MacOS.
